description: Run one named agent or a concurrent `tasks[]` batch, each with its own prompt, tools and on-disk history. The agent definition is <agent_name>.md (or <agent_name>) searched in the project, profile and installation .agents//agents/ directories, plugin agents/ directories and skills/<skill_name>/agents/; `agent_name` is required for a single run and may be the batch default. The definition's front matter may pin model, toolsets, enable_tools, max_iterations, reasoning_effort, worktree, output, spawns, blocking and the skip flags; a caller argument overrides it (blocking: true forces an inline run). `spawn` is a one-call shorthand: `spawn:@<agent_name>` on the first line, then the task body. By default the run is background and the answer arrives as a completion; background=false blocks and returns the answer. A background run that is not blocking/worktree stays resident after it settles (agent_sessions.keep_alive): it keeps its slot until the idle TTL parks it, a message wakes it, and a parked one revives on the next message. Every call is a new agent session with its own transcript at <parent bundle>/<topic>.jsonl under the profile's sessions/ tree (a run with no parent session gets its own bundle); the payload returns agent_session_id and subject, which agent_out reads back. Runs do not continue each other implicitly: pass continue_from with a prior agent_session_id to carry that conversation forward.
name: agent

agent_name.description: The agent's name (a file name, not a path); also its history folder.

background.description: true (default) returns jobs and delivers answers later, dispatching a batch concurrently; false blocks and runs the call (or every task in a batch, in array order) on the calling thread.

context.description: Shared batch context (`# Goal`, `# Contract` interfaces), prepended to every task prompt; NEVER repeat it per task.

context_files.description: Files to supply as data (at most 20, 100KB each, 200KB total). A path is project-relative (or absolute inside the project/profile home), and `local://<path>` is an accepted spelling of the same reference.

continue_from.description: A prior agent_session_id whose transcript seeds this run's history. The new run still gets its own id, subject and transcript.

effort.description: Coarse reasoning effort; maps to low/medium/high.

enable_tools.description: Explicit tool-name allowlist. When non-empty it replaces tool_sets and the definition's toolsets; every name must be a registered tool (an unknown name fails closed). Host-only extra tools cannot be named.

independent_completions.description: Batch background runs: true (default) delivers one completion per task; false buffers them into one combined completion.

isolated.description: Alias for worktree (isolated git worktree per run).

load_soul_identity.description: Load the operator soul/system identity (default false).

max_iterations.description: Per-run tool-call budget; overrides the definition and host default.

model.description: Pin the route as 'provider:model', a bare model name, or '@role' (@default, @task, @advisor or an auxiliary.<task> slot such as @smol).

name.description: Profile-unique short name (CamelCase letters/digits, at most 32) that agent_message and agent_out address this session by. Generated from the agent name plus four hex characters when omitted; a duplicate is refused.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema the final answer must satisfy; overrides the definition's output contract for this call.

project_dir.description: Working directory for the run; defaults to the project root.

schema_mode.description: permissive (default) returns the raw answer after a failed validation; strict fails the run instead.

skill_name.description: Optional skill folder whose skills/<skill_name>/agents/ is searched.

skip_background_review.description: Skip the post-turn background review fork (default true).

skip_context_files.description: Skip project context files such as AGENTS.md (default true).

skip_memory.description: Skip host memory context (default true for a named peer).

spawn.description: One-call shorthand: 'spawn:@<agent_name>' on the first line, then the task body. Mutually exclusive with agent_name, user_prompts, task_file and tasks; the named agent still passes the caller's spawns allow-list and depth limit.

subject.description: One-line topic for this agent session; unique, and how agent_out finds it. Defaults to the first line of user_prompts.

system_prompts.description: System prompt used only when no agent definition file is found in the search path.

task_file.description: Read the prompt from this file instead of user_prompts (absolute or project-relative, inside the project or profile home).

tasks.description: Batch form: one object per agent. With background=false (or a blocking definition) tasks run one at a time in array order on the calling thread; background tasks are dispatched concurrently. Each item takes `agent` (defaults to agent_name), `user_prompts` (or `task`), and may override name, subject, model, tool_sets, enable_tools/tools, context_files, worktree/isolated, output_schema, continue_from, background.

agent.description: Agent definition name for this task.

solution_space.description: How open-ended the problem is; appended to the prompt.

user_prompts.description: The task prompt; `task` is accepted as an alias.

tool_sets.description: Toolsets for this run, limited to the default-loaded built-in sets; omit for that default, or ['*'] for every host tool.

tools.description: Alias for enable_tools; pass only one of the two.

user_prompts.description: The user message for this run (a list is joined with blank lines).

worktree.description: Run in an isolated git worktree off HEAD; the run's edits are committed and merged back automatically (apply=auto). A dirty parent workspace, a merge conflict or a failed merge keeps the branch and reports why. Off by default; degrades to the shared workspace outside git or on a non-local terminal backend, and the payload says which happened.
